Plan to identify individual borough-level hot and cold spots

1. Load the two CSV files into pandas data frames:  
   a) NO2_Q2_2023.csv  → columns: borough, NO2_µg_m³  
   b) borough_adjacency.csv → columns: borough, neighbor (one row per edge).

2. Handle the six missing NO2 values:  
   • Drop those borough records entirely from the analysis.  
   • Also drop any links in the adjacency list that involve a dropped borough, so every unit kept has a complete set of valid neighbours.  
   (Reason: imputing would inject artificial spatial structure; list-wise deletion preserves the integrity of the permutation test.)

3. Build the spatial weights matrix W:  
   • For each remaining borough i, set w_ij = 1 if j is listed as a neighbour after step 2, else 0.  
   • Row-standardise: divide each row by its row sum so Σ_j w_ij = 1 (needed for Local Moran’s I).

4. Compute data vectors:  
   • x_i  = NO2 value for borough i.  
   • x̄    = mean(x).  
   • S²   = variance(x) across the retained boroughs.

5. Calculate the observed Local Moran’s I for every borough:  
      I_i = (x_i − x̄) · Σ_j w_ij (x_j − x̄) / S²

6. Significance test (no external spatial libraries):  
   • Permutation approach with 999 random shuffles (>500 as required).  
   • For each shuffle k, randomly permute the NO2 values among boroughs, recompute I_i^k.  
   • p-value_i = ( # permutations where |I_i^k| ≥ |I_i| ) / 1000  (include observed in denominator).  
   • Borough is significant if p-value_i < 0.05.

7. Classify significant boroughs:  
   • HOT SPOT (HH) if:  
       – x_i > x̄ (above-average NO2) AND  
       – p-value_i < 0.05 AND  
       – I_i is positive.  
   • COLD SPOT (LL) if:  
       – x_i < x̄ (below-average NO2) AND  
       – p-value_i < 0.05 AND  
       – I_i is positive.  
   (Positive I_i indicates the borough matches its neighbours; the sign of x_i − x̄ tells whether it is high or low.)

8. Compile the results:  
   • For every borough meeting HH or LL criteria, record the borough name, tag (HH or LL), and its observed I_i value (rounded reasonably).  
   • If none meet the criteria, report “none”.

9. Output exactly one line:  
   FINAL ANSWER: Borough1 (HH, I=<value>), Borough2 (LL, I=<value>), ...

- HOT SPOT: a borough with a high NO2 air pollution that is ALSO surrounded by other high-NO2 air pollution neighboring boroughs
- COLD SPOT: a borough with a low NO2 air pollution that is ALSO surrounded by other low-NO2 air pollution neighboring boroughs

Look at each borough together with its neighbors from the adjacency list, and identify any that qualify. Explain your reasoning, including a computed value for each borough you name. Note: dedicated spatial-statistics packages (pysal, esda, libpysal, geopandas, or similar) are NOT installed in this environment -- don't spend turns trying different import paths for them. For implementation including statistical method such as Moran's I, directly use only pandas and numpy. If you test statistical significance via a permutation/randomization test, use at least 500 random shuffles -- fewer permutations can produce an unstable p-value that lands on the wrong side of the 0.05 threshold just by chance, especially when the true effect is only moderate.

End your response with exactly one line listing every borough you identified, using HH for hot spot and LL for cold spot, and including a computed value for each:
FINAL ANSWER: BoroughName1 (HH, statistical method=<value>), BoroughName2 (LL, statistical method =<value>), ...

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. LOAD DATA
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
NO2_PATH = "chunks_csv/moran_local_no2crime_no2_Q2_2023.csv"
ADJ_PATH = "chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv"

no2 = pd.read_csv(NO2_PATH)            # columns: borough, value
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJ_PATH)            # columns: borough, neighbor

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. DROP BOROUGHS WITH MISSING NO2 + CLEAN ADJACENCY
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
no2_clean = no2.dropna(subset=["value"]).reset_index(drop=True)
valid_boroughs = set(no2_clean["borough"])

adj_clean = adj[adj["borough"].isin(valid_boroughs) & 
                adj["neighbor"].isin(valid_boroughs)].copy()

# add the reverse direction to make sure adjacency is symmetric
rev = adj_clean.rename(columns={"borough":"neighbor", "neighbor":"borough"})
adj_undirected = pd.concat([adj_clean, rev], ignore_index=True).drop_duplicates()

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. BUILD NEIGHBOUR LIST & WEIGHT MATRIX
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
neighbors = {b:set() for b in valid_boroughs}
for _, row in adj_undirected.iterrows():
    neighbors[row["borough"]].add(row["neighbor"])

# drop any borough that (after NA-cleaning) has zero neighbours
neighbors = {k:v for k,v in neighbors.items() if len(v)>0}
kept_boroughs = list(neighbors.keys())
no2_kept = no2_clean[no2_clean["borough"].isin(kept_boroughs)].set_index("borough").loc[kept_boroughs]

x = no2_kept["value"].values.astype(float)
x_bar = x.mean()
S2 = x.var()          # population variance, ddof=0
n = len(kept_boroughs)

# pre-compute deviation from mean for speed
dev = x - x_bar

# row-standardised weights as a dict of arrays
weight_rows = []
for b in kept_boroughs:
    row = np.zeros(n, dtype=float)
    neigh_set = neighbors[b]
    if len(neigh_set):
        w = 1.0/len(neigh_set)
        for neigh in neigh_set:
            j = kept_boroughs.index(neigh)
            row[j] = w
    weight_rows.append(row)

W = np.array(weight_rows)        # shape (n,n)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. LOCAL MORAN'S I (OBSERVED)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# For each i: I_i = (x_i - x̄) * Σ_j w_ij (x_j - x̄) / S²
I_obs = (dev * (W @ dev)) / S2

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. PERMUTATION TEST
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
n_perm = 999
counts = np.ones(n, dtype=int)   # start at 1 to include observed itself

for _ in range(n_perm):
    perm = np.random.permutation(x)
    perm_dev = perm - x_bar
    I_perm = (perm_dev * (W @ perm_dev)) / S2
    counts += (np.abs(I_perm) >= np.abs(I_obs))

p_vals = counts / (n_perm + 1)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. CLASSIFY BOROUGHS
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
hotspots = []
coldspots = []

for i, b in enumerate(kept_boroughs):
    if p_vals[i] < 0.05 and I_obs[i] > 0:
        if x[i] > x_bar:
            hotspots.append((b, I_obs[i], p_vals[i]))
        elif x[i] < x_bar:
            coldspots.append((b, I_obs[i], p_vals[i]))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. PRINT REQUIRED LINES
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
data_points_used = n
print(f"data_points_used = {data_points_used}")

if len(hotspots)+len(coldspots)==0:
    final_string = "FINAL ANSWER: none"
else:
    pieces = []
    for b, I_val, p in hotspots:
        pieces.append(f"{b} (HH, I={I_val:.3f}, p={p:.3f})")
    for b, I_val, p in coldspots:
        pieces.append(f"{b} (LL, I={I_val:.3f}, p={p:.3f})")
    final_string = "FINAL ANSWER: " + ", ".join(pieces)

print(final_string)

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load data
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
DATA_PATH = "chunks_csv/moran_local_no2crime_no2_Q2_2023.csv"
ADJ_PATH  = "chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv"

no2 = pd.read_csv(DATA_PATH)           # columns: borough, value
adj  = pd.read_csv(ADJ_PATH)           # columns: borough, neighbor

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Drop boroughs with missing NO2 values
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
valid_no2 = no2.dropna(subset=['value']).reset_index(drop=True)
kept_boroughs = set(valid_no2['borough'])

# clean adjacency to contain only kept boroughs
adj_clean = adj[adj['borough'].isin(kept_boroughs) & adj['neighbor'].isin(kept_boroughs)]

# build neighbor list dictionary
neighbor_dict = {b: [] for b in kept_boroughs}
for _, row in adj_clean.iterrows():
    neighbor_dict[row['borough']].append(row['neighbor'])
    neighbor_dict[row['neighbor']].append(row['borough'])  # ensure symmetry

# drop any borough that ended up with zero neighbours (if any)
neighbor_dict = {b: nbrs for b, nbrs in neighbor_dict.items() if len(nbrs) > 0}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Prepare vectors/mappings
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
boroughs = list(neighbor_dict.keys())
index_of = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(boroughs)}

x = np.array([valid_no2.loc[valid_no2['borough'] == b, 'value'].values[0] 
              for b in boroughs], dtype=float)

x_bar = x.mean()
S2 = np.var(x, ddof=0)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Build row-standardised weights
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# weights[i] is tuple(list_of_indices, list_of_weights)
weights = []
for b in boroughs:
    nbrs = neighbor_dict[b]
    idxs = [index_of[n] for n in nbrs]
    w = [1.0/len(idxs)]*len(idxs)           # row-standardised
    weights.append((idxs, w))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Observed Local Moran's I
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
def local_I(i, values):
    xi = values[i] - x_bar
    nbr_idxs, wts = weights[i]
    spatial_lag = sum(wt * (values[j] - x_bar) for j, wt in zip(nbr_idxs, wts))
    return (xi * spatial_lag) / S2

I_obs = np.array([local_I(i, x) for i in range(len(boroughs))])

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Permutation test (999 permutations  -> 1000 including observed)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
n_perm = 999
greater_equal = np.zeros(len(boroughs), dtype=int)

rng = np.random.default_rng(seed=42)  # reproducibility
for _ in range(n_perm):
    permuted = rng.permutation(x)
    I_perm = np.array([local_I(i, permuted) for i in range(len(boroughs))])
    greater_equal += (np.abs(I_perm) >= np.abs(I_obs))

p_values = (greater_equal + 1) / (n_perm + 1)   # +1 to include observed

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Classify hotspots (HH) and coldspots (LL)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
mean_val = x_bar
results = []
for b, I_i, p_i, val in zip(boroughs, I_obs, p_values, x):
    if (p_i < 0.05) and (I_i > 0):     # significant clustering
        if val > mean_val:
            tag = 'HH'
        elif val < mean_val:
            tag = 'LL'
        else:
            continue
        results.append((b, tag, I_i, p_i))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Output
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
data_points_used = len(boroughs)
print(f"data_points_used = {data_points_used}")

if results:
    parts = [f"{b} ({tag}, I={I_val:.4f}, p={p_val:.4f})"
             for b, tag, I_val, p_val in results]
    final_answer = "FINAL ANSWER: " + ", ".join(parts)
else:
    final_answer = "FINAL ANSWER: none"

# ensure the FINAL ANSWER line references computed 'final_answer'
print(f"{final_answer}")

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load data
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
DATA_PATH = "chunks_csv/moran_local_no2crime_no2_Q2_2023.csv"
ADJ_PATH   = "chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv"

no2 = pd.read_csv(DATA_PATH)           # columns: borough, value
edges = pd.read_csv(ADJ_PATH)          # columns: borough, neighbor

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Drop boroughs whose NO₂ value is missing
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
valid_no2 = no2.dropna(subset=["value"]).reset_index(drop=True)     # 33 – 6 = 27 left
valid_boros = set(valid_no2['borough'])

# prune the edge list so that every endpoint still exists
edges = edges[edges['borough'].isin(valid_boros) & edges['neighbor'].isin(valid_boros)]

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Build a row-standardised binary spatial‐weights matrix  W
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
#   * give the remaining boroughs a numerical index for fast array math
indexer = {b:i for i,b in enumerate(valid_no2['borough'])}
n = len(valid_no2)

rows, cols, data = [], [], []
for b, neigh in edges.itertuples(index=False):
    i, j = indexer[b], indexer[neigh]
    rows.append(i); cols.append(j); data.append(1)

# put into a dense matrix because n=27 is tiny
W = np.zeros((n, n))
for r,c in zip(rows, cols):
    W[r, c] = 1

# drop any borough that (after pruning) is left with NO neighbours
row_sums = W.sum(axis=1)
keep_idx = np.where(row_sums > 0)[0]
if len(keep_idx) < n:                     # if we lost some, update everything
    valid_no2 = valid_no2.iloc[keep_idx].reset_index(drop=True)
    indexer   = {b:i for i,b in enumerate(valid_no2['borough'])}
    # rebuild W only with kept nodes
    n = len(valid_no2)
    W = np.zeros((n, n))
    for b, neigh in edges.itertuples(index=False):
        if b in indexer and neigh in indexer:
            i, j = indexer[b], indexer[neigh]
            W[i, j] = 1
    row_sums = W.sum(axis=1)

# row-standardise: each non-empty row sums to 1
W = W / row_sums[:, None]

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Standardise NO₂ values  (z-scores)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
x = valid_no2['value'].values.astype(float)
z = (x - x.mean()) / x.std(ddof=0)          # population σ so variance=1 exactly

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Local Moran’s I  (row-standardised version)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
I_obs = z * (W @ z)                         # shape: (n,)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Monte-Carlo significance test (999 permutations)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
n_perm = 999
rng = np.random.default_rng(seed=0)

perm_I = np.empty((n_perm, n))
for p in range(n_perm):
    z_perm = rng.permutation(z)
    perm_I[p] = z_perm * (W @ z_perm)

# two-sided pseudo-p
p_vals = (np.sum(np.abs(perm_I) >= np.abs(I_obs), axis=0) + 1) / (n_perm + 1)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Classify boroughs
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
results = []
for i, (bor, zi, Ii, pv) in enumerate(zip(valid_no2['borough'], z, I_obs, p_vals)):
    if pv < 0.05 and Ii > 0:
        tag = "HH" if zi > 0 else "LL"
        if zi == 0:     # exactly on mean – shouldn’t happen with continuous data
            continue
        results.append((bor, tag, Ii, pv))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Produce the required prints
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
data_points_used = len(valid_no2)
print(f"data_points_used = {data_points_used}")

if results:
    formatted = ", ".join([f"{b} ({t}, I={I:.3f}, p={p:.3f})"
                           for b,t,I,p in results])
    print(f"FINAL ANSWER: {formatted}")
else:
    print("FINAL ANSWER: none")
